title: EchoForge canonical summary, versions 1-3
description: One immutable summary revision, generated from one exact transcript revision. Every factual item carries evidence: the pair transcript_revision + segment_id, plus times EchoForge derived from that segment rather than took from model output. A summary is a reviewable draft, not an unquestionable record, and the schema is built so that an unsupported claim cannot be represented as a supported one. Version 3 adds the meeting brief: an ordered action plan, and sections that keep speculative ideas out of the list of things somebody has to do. Versions 1 and 2 remain readable exactly as they were written and are never rewritten in place.

transcript_revision.description: The revision this summary was written from. Half of every evidence identity: a bare segment ID is stable only inside one revision and is not a durable reference.

transcript_sha256.description: Digest of the transcript revision, so 'the transcript changed underneath this summary' is detectable rather than assumed.

meeting_date.description: The calendar date of the meeting, when it is known. Null means relative dates such as 'Friday' cannot be resolved and must stay unknown.

repair_attempt.description: 0 when this document was generated first time, 1 when the first answer was refused and it was generated once more. At most one re-ask is allowed: a model told what was wrong with an unsupported answer will often produce a supported one, but asking repeatedly is how a generator eventually stumbles onto output that satisfies the checks without satisfying the transcript. A repair is another chance to answer, never a lower bar to clear - the same validator judges both.

synthesis.description: How the extracted facts were folded together. A meeting long enough to exceed one pass is merged hierarchically, and the shape of that fold is recorded rather than left implicit: a reader who wonders why two near-identical decisions both survived is owed the answer that they were never considered side by side. Null in documents written before the fold was recorded.

levels.description: Passes over the facts. 1 for a meeting that fitted in one.

groups.description: Groups folded across all passes. Never fewer than levels.

reached_level_cap.description: True when the fold stopped at its backstop. It stops holding everything it had - nothing is ever dropped to make the result fit - so this is a note about effort, not about completeness.

narrative.description: Evidence-grounded final prose. Null for schema-v1 history and for the explicitly labelled placeholder.

brief.description: The document a person reads after the meeting. Null for schema-v1/v2 history and for the explicitly labelled placeholder. Sections are omitted when the meeting has nothing for them: a brief that prints an empty Risks heading every time teaches the reader to skim past the one meeting where it says something.

future_ideas.description: Wanted eventually rather than now. Absent in v1/v2 history, where a speculative aside and an assignment for tomorrow landed in the same list.

important_context.description: Worth remembering, and not itself work.

dependencies.description: 'A has to happen before B', as the meeting stated it. What lets the plan be ordered without inventing an order.

certainty.description: How well the transcript supports this. 'explicit' requires direct supporting text; 'inferred' is a reading of it and is shown separately; 'unknown' is the honest answer when the transcript does not say. Final synthesis may never raise one of these.

produces_summaries.description: False for any placeholder backend. A false value must be surfaced, never hidden: placeholder prose is not a summary of anything that was said.

run.description: Content-free performance and fallback telemetry. It contains no transcript, prompt, or summary prose.

evidence.description: One citation. The identity is the pair transcript_revision + segment_id; the times are derived by EchoForge from that segment and are never taken from model output.

confidence.description: A model's own number, which is not statistically calibrated. Labelled heuristic everywhere it is shown, and never the basis for certainty.

supported_item.description: An item that may never be emitted without a citation, whatever its certainty. Decisions are the things people act on afterwards.

plan_basis.description: Why a step says what it says. 'explicit' is something the meeting stated; 'grounded_inference' is a relationship it implied strongly enough to act on - 'do A before B' when the meeting said B needs A; 'recommendation' is EchoForge ordering work the meeting left unordered. Keeping them apart is what lets the brief be useful about sequencing without presenting sequencing as something somebody said.

plan_step.description: One numbered step of the action plan. Ordered as one sequence and split by audience only for display, so that two lists can never disagree about what comes first.

audience.description: 'you' is the microphone holder, 'others' is somebody named as doing the work, 'unassigned' is real work nobody claimed - the normal case in real meetings, and not a gap to fill.

timing.description: Taken from the meeting - a stated deadline, a customer demo, an unresolved prerequisite, an explicit 'not now' - and never from generic business assumptions.

allOf.description: An unknown owner is null here for the same reason it is on an action item.
A step addressed to somebody else has to name them.

due_date.description: An ISO date, emitted only when the transcript gives an unambiguous calendar date relative to a known meeting date.

due_date_text.description: What was actually said - 'by Friday', 'end of the month'. Kept even when no date could be resolved.

classification.description: How this commitment relates to the meeting. 'Stop the recording' and 'Andy will give Storm access' are both imperative sentences somebody said; only one is work that exists once the call ends. Absent in v1/v2 history, where every imperative sentence became an action item. Only post_meeting_commitment and inferred_next_step ever reach the action plan.

allOf.description: An unknown owner is null. There is no such thing as an unknown owner with a name.
An explicit owner has to be a name the transcript actually gives.
